title: One partition, or none
prompt: This program asks for the smallest sensible number of partitions, then for none at all. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
one = api_requests.repartition(1)
print(one.rdd.getNumPartitions(), one.count())
try:
    api_requests.repartition(0)
    print("made it")
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__)
hints: `repartition(1)` puts every row in one partition; rows are never lost.
Every task works on one partition. Can a DataFrame have zero partitions to work on?
Spark checks the number when you call `repartition`, before any rows are read, and raises an error that names a bad argument.
explanation: `repartition(1)` gives one partition holding all 12 requests. Asking for 0 partitions is refused straight away with `IllegalArgumentException`, because the number must be positive, so `made it` is never printed.
